binding_resolver_inverted.vector: the report admits WorldForge resolved the subject

binding_substituted_anchor_actor.vector: WorldForge surveyed a different actor than the one named and reported success

binding_substituted_map.vector: right subject id, wrong level — still not the survey that was asked for

binding_transform_beyond_tolerance.vector: anchor drift of ~1.56cm Euclidean — under 1cm on every single axis, and still outside the L2 tolerance. The per-axis reading of this rail is the trap this fixture exists to catch

binding_wrong_subject_id.vector: a real survey of the wrong subject, returned against this request

cleanup_package_dirty_after_cleanup.vector: every temporary object was destroyed and witnessed gone, and the survey STILL left the map package dirty. The ledger conjunct is satisfied here, so a rejection proves the snapshot term is doing its own work

cleanup_temporary_marker_left_behind.vector: a temporary object the survey spawned, reported destroyed, and then OBSERVED still present after cleanup. Both inventory snapshots agree — the object was created and removed between them as far as any set comparison can tell — so only the per-object ledger can see it

operation_replayed_from_another_request.residual_gap: caught on the OPERATION-IDENTITY axis, not from the report body. The runtime report's operation block does carry request_hash (run_scene_survey_probe.py:1405-1408) but no validator reads it, so a copy presented WITHOUT its manifest is still undetectable from the report alone
operation_replayed_from_another_request.vector: a prior operation's report and manifest re-presented for a NEW asking. The question is byte-identical, so request_hash matches perfectly — only the operation id betrays the replay, which is precisely why it is excluded from the hash

operation_request_hash_mismatch.vector: evidence sealed against one question, presented against another — same operation id, different map. The manifest's own seal is intact; only the binding to THIS request is false

operation_wrong_target_commit.residual_gap: same shape as the repository case: target_commit is hashed (scene_survey_operation.py:587) so evidence sealed against a different commit is refused, but nothing verifies the far side actually ran at that commit. Only the live-bridge path shape-checks 40-hex (tools/bridge/live.py:146-150)
operation_wrong_target_commit.vector: a survey of one commit handed back against a request naming another

operation_wrong_target_repository.residual_gap: target_repository is a caller ASSERTION that nothing resolves. The rail below refuses evidence sealed against a different asserted repository (it is in REQUEST_HASH_INCLUDED, scene_survey_operation.py:591), but no scene-survey code observes which tree was actually surveyed — scene_survey_far_side.py never resolves a repository at all. The live bridge's field comparison (tools/bridge/live.py:141-145, WF1024) has no scene-survey counterpart
operation_wrong_target_repository.vector: a survey of one repository handed back against a request naming another

report_clean_without_evidence.vector: a clean pass with no evidence behind it

report_dry_probe_claims_runtime.vector: a report that never executed claiming live runtime truth

report_executed_without_observed_anchor.vector: an executed run that cannot say where it actually looked

report_pre_wave1_scratch_shape.vector: the pre-Wave-1 report shape, which predates subject binding entirely and would silently satisfy a gate that only asked whether a report exists

report_resolver_inverted.vector: a report asserting WorldForge chose the subject

report_unknown_failure_code.vector: a failure code invented to look rigorous

report_valid_exceeds_total.vector: more valid samples than were ever taken

report_zero_support_samples_passed.vector: a pass built on zero probed support samples

subject_both_anchor_channels.vector: both anchor channels populated — WorldForge would have to pick one

subject_empty_subject_id.vector: a blank subject id — nothing to bind a report back to

subject_missing_anchor_mode.vector: a subject that never says how its anchor is expressed

subject_missing_map.vector: a subject with no map — WorldForge would have to choose the level

subject_neither_anchor_channel.vector: neither anchor channel populated — the caller never resolved the subject

subject_resolved_by_worldforge.vector: a subject WorldForge claims to have resolved itself — the exact authority inversion v2.6 exists to refuse

subject_unknown_key.vector: an extra key smuggled onto the subject

subject_wrong_schema_version.vector: a subject claiming a schema version this build does not implement

not_yet_testable.nondeterministic_repeated_reports: requires two real editor runs; determinism is enforced at runtime from per_run_hashes, which no static fixture can produce honestly
not_yet_testable.screenshot_without_runtime_evidence: no screenshot artifact is produced at all under the current -nullrhi pass, so the vector has no on-disk form yet
not_yet_testable.subject_binding_hash_mismatch: subject_binding_hash does not exist anywhere in this build: no writer, no reader, no compute helper, and no slot in REPORT_ALLOWED (scene_survey_contracts.py:662-680), so strict check_no_unknown would reject it outright if a fixture invented one. The subject IS covered transitively — 'subject' is in REQUEST_HASH_INCLUDED (scene_survey_operation.py:586) — but that is the request hash, not a subject-binding hash, and a fixture that renamed one to the other would be testing a field this build has never had

note: Fixtures carry no harness metadata on purpose: an embedded _expected_code key would itself be rejected by the strict unknown-key rail, which looks green and proves nothing.
